question: Select two facilities from five potential locations (Node 0, Node 1, Node 2, Node 3, and Node 4) to maximize the minimum distance between any two selected facilities. Each location can either be selected (1) or not selected (0). For every pair of locations, determine whether both are selected as facilities, represented by a binary decision variable. The distances between the locations are scaled by a factor of 1,000,000 and are as follows: Node 0 and Node 1: 19 units, Node 0 and Node 2: 21 units, Node 0 and Node 3: 31 units, Node 0 and Node 4: 35 units, Node 1 and Node 0: 29 units, Node 1 and Node 2: 13 units, Node 1 and Node 3: 46 units, Node 1 and Node 4: 37 units, Node 2 and Node 0: 50 units, Node 2 and Node 1: 22 units, Node 2 and Node 3: 49 units, Node 2 and Node 4: 33 units, Node 3 and Node 0: 18 units, Node 3 and Node 1: 20 units, Node 3 and Node 2: 46 units, Node 3 and Node 4: 33 units, Node 4 and Node 0: 18 units, Node 4 and Node 1: 26 units, Node 4 and Node 2: 39 units, Node 4 and Node 3: 43 units. The total number of selected facilities must equal two. For every pair of locations, the selection of both facilities in the pair is only possible if both individual facilities are selected, enforced through constraints linking the pairwise selection variables to the individual facility selection variables. All decision variables are binary, ensuring facilities are either fully selected or not selected at all. The objective is to maximize the minimum distance between any two selected facilities, ensuring geographical dispersion while adhering to the constraints on pairwise selection and total facility count.

    "scale": 1000000,
    # ordered-pair distances (raw units); scaled inside model via DATA["scale"]
    "dist": {
        (0, 1): 19, (0, 2): 21, (0, 3): 31, (0, 4): 35,
        (1, 0): 29, (1, 2): 13, (1, 3): 46, (1, 4): 37,
        (2, 0): 50, (2, 1): 22, (2, 3): 49, (2, 4): 33,
        (3, 0): 18, (3, 1): 20, (3, 2): 46, (3, 4): 33,
        (4, 0): 18, (4, 1): 26, (4, 2): 39, (4, 3): 43,
    },
    # big-M for the min-distance linearisation (larger than any scaled distance)
    "big_m": 100000000,
}

GOLD_ANSWER = None


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA
    nodes = d["nodes"]
    dist = d["dist"]
    scale = d["scale"]
    pairs = list(dist.keys())
    big_m = d["big_m"]

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    model.N = pyo.Set(initialize=nodes)
    model.P = pyo.Set(initialize=pairs, dimen=2)

    # facility selection
    model.select = pyo.Var(model.N, within=pyo.Binary)

    # pairwise selection indicator
    model.pair = pyo.Var(model.P, within=pyo.Binary)

    # minimum distance among selected facilities (scaled)
    model.min_dist = pyo.Var(within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    # exactly two facilities
    def count_rule(m):
        return sum(m.select[i] for i in m.N) == d["num_facilities"]
    model.num_facilities = pyo.Constraint(rule=count_rule)

    # pair[i,j] <= select[i]
    def pair_le_i_rule(m, i, j):
        return m.pair[i, j] <= m.select[i]
    model.pair_le_first = pyo.Constraint(model.P, rule=pair_le_i_rule)

    # pair[i,j] <= select[j]
    def pair_le_j_rule(m, i, j):
        return m.pair[i, j] <= m.select[j]
    model.pair_le_second = pyo.Constraint(model.P, rule=pair_le_j_rule)

    # pair[i,j] >= select[i] + select[j] - 1  (chosen pair becomes active)
    def pair_ge_rule(m, i, j):
        return m.pair[i, j] >= m.select[i] + m.select[j] - 1
    model.pair_lower = pyo.Constraint(model.P, rule=pair_ge_rule)

    # min_dist <= dist[i,j] + M*(1 - pair[i,j])
    def min_dist_rule(m, i, j):
        return m.min_dist <= dist[i, j] * scale + big_m * (1 - m.pair[i, j])
    model.min_dist_link = pyo.Constraint(model.P, rule=min_dist_rule)

    # objective: maximise the minimum pairwise distance
    model.obj = pyo.Objective(expr=model.min_dist, sense=pyo.maximize)

    return model

DATA = {
    # "Select two facilities from five potential locations (Node 0..4)"
    "locations": [0, 1, 2, 3, 4],
    # "The total number of selected facilities must equal two."
    "num_selected": 2,
    # "The distances ... are scaled by a factor of 1,000,000"
    "scale": 1_000_000,
    # Raw distances (units) for each ordered pair, from the problem statement.
    "dist_raw": {
        (0, 1): 19, (0, 2): 21, (0, 3): 31, (0, 4): 35,
        (1, 0): 29, (1, 2): 13, (1, 3): 46, (1, 4): 37,
        (2, 0): 50, (2, 1): 22, (2, 3): 49, (2, 4): 33,
        (3, 0): 18, (3, 1): 20, (3, 2): 46, (3, 4): 33,
        (4, 0): 18, (4, 1): 26, (4, 2): 39, (4, 3): 43,
    },
    # Big-M: larger than any scaled distance (scale * max_raw). Kept in DATA.
    "big_m": 1_000_000 * 50,
}


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA

    locations = d["locations"]
    pairs = list(d["dist_raw"].keys())
    scaled = {k: v * d["scale"] for k, v in d["dist_raw"].items()}

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    model.N = pyo.Set(initialize=locations)
    model.P = pyo.Set(initialize=pairs, dimen=2)

    # y[i]: 1 if facility i is selected
    model.y = pyo.Var(model.N, within=pyo.Binary)

    # z[i,j]: 1 if both i and j are selected
    model.z = pyo.Var(model.P, within=pyo.Binary)

    # D: the minimum distance among selected facility pairs
    model.D = pyo.Var(within=pyo.NonNegativeReals,
                      bounds=(0, d["big_m"]))

    # Exactly two facilities selected
    def total_rule(m):
        return sum(m.y[i] for i in m.N) == d["num_selected"]
    model.total = pyo.Constraint(rule=total_rule)

    # Linking: z[i,j] <= y[i]
    def link_i_rule(m, i, j):
        return m.z[i, j] <= m.y[i]
    model.link_i = pyo.Constraint(model.P, rule=link_i_rule)

    # Linking: z[i,j] <= y[j]
    def link_j_rule(m, i, j):
        return m.z[i, j] <= m.y[j]
    model.link_j = pyo.Constraint(model.P, rule=link_j_rule)

    # Minimum-distance definition: D <= dist[i,j] + M(1 - z[i,j])
    def min_dist_rule(m, i, j):
        return m.D <= scaled[(i, j)] + d["big_m"] * (1 - m.z[i, j])
    model.min_dist = pyo.Constraint(model.P, rule=min_dist_rule)

    # Objective: maximize the minimum distance
    model.obj = pyo.Objective(expr=model.D, sense=pyo.maximize)

    return model

def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA
    nodes = d["nodes"]
    pairs = list(d["dist"].keys())
    M = d["bigM"]

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()
    model.N = pyo.Set(initialize=nodes)
    model.P = pyo.Set(initialize=pairs, dimen=2)

    # x[i] = 1 if facility i selected
    model.x = pyo.Var(model.N, within=pyo.Binary, bounds=(0, 1))
    # z[i,j] = 1 if both i and j selected (co-selected pair)
    model.z = pyo.Var(model.P, within=pyo.Binary, bounds=(0, 1))
    # D = minimum pairwise distance among selected facilities
    model.D = pyo.Var(within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    # Exactly p facilities selected
    def count_rule(m):
        return sum(m.x[i] for i in m.N) == d["p"]
    model.count = pyo.Constraint(rule=count_rule)

    # Link z[i,j] <= x[i] : pair co-selection requires i selected
    def z_le_xi_rule(m, i, j):
        return m.z[i, j] <= m.x[i]
    model.z_le_xi = pyo.Constraint(model.P, rule=z_le_xi_rule)

    # Link z[i,j] <= x[j] : pair co-selection requires j selected
    def z_le_xj_rule(m, i, j):
        return m.z[i, j] <= m.x[j]
    model.z_le_xj = pyo.Constraint(model.P, rule=z_le_xj_rule)

    # Co-selection consistency: sum over j of z[i,j] = x[i]*(p-1) when x[i]=1.
    def pair_sum_rule(m, i):
        total = sum(m.z[a, b] for (a, b) in m.P if a == i)
        return total == (d["p"] - 1) * m.x[i]
    model.pair_sum = pyo.Constraint(model.N, rule=pair_sum_rule)

    # Big-M: D <= dist[i,j] * z[i,j] + M*(1 - z[i,j]) for every pair.
    def d_bound_rule(m, i, j):
        return m.D <= d["dist"][(i, j)] * m.z[i, j] + M * (1 - m.z[i, j])
    model.d_bound = pyo.Constraint(model.P, rule=d_bound_rule)

    # Maximize the minimum pairwise distance
    model.obj = pyo.Objective(expr=model.D, sense=pyo.maximize)

    return model

import pyomo.environ as pyo

DATA = {
    # number of facilities to select
    "num_facilities": 2,
    # maximum scaled distance magnitude for big-M
    "scale": 1000000,
    "num_nodes": 5,
    # directed distances in units scaled by 1e6 (raw units are the numbers given)
    "dist": {
        (0, 1): 19, (0, 2): 21, (0, 3): 31, (0, 4): 35,
        (1, 0): 29, (1, 2): 13, (1, 3): 46, (1, 4): 37,
        (2, 0): 50, (2, 1): 22, (2, 3): 49, (2, 4): 33,
        (3, 0): 18, (3, 1): 20, (3, 2): 46, (3, 4): 33,
        (4, 0): 18, (4, 1): 26, (4, 2): 22 if False else 39, (4, 3): 43,
    }
}


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA
    n = d["num_nodes"]
    scale = d["scale"]

    nodes = list(range(n))
    pairs = [(i, j) for i in nodes for j in nodes if i < j]

    m = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    m.I = pyo.Set(initialize=nodes)
    # Pair set indexed by an integer k with mapping to (i,j)
    m.P = pyo.Set(initialize=range(len(pairs)), ordered=True)
    pair_map = dict(enumerate(pairs))

    # Derived data constant: big-M, larger than max scaled distance
    max_dist_scaled = max(d["dist"].values()) * scale
    M = max_dist_scaled + 1

    m.y = pyo.Var(m.I, within=pyo.Binary)
    m.p = pyo.Var(m.P, within=pyo.Binary)
    m.D = pyo.Var(within=pyo.NonNegativeReals, bounds=(0, max_dist_scaled))

    # Exactly num_facilities selected
    m.exact_count = pyo.Constraint(
        expr=sum(m.y[i] for i in m.I) == d["num_facilities"]
    )

    def link_lower_rule(mm, k):
        i, j = pair_map[k]
        return mm.p[k] <= mm.y[i]

    def link_upper_rule(mm, k):
        i, j = pair_map[k]
        return mm.p[k] <= mm.y[j]

    def link_both_rule(mm, k):
        i, j = pair_map[k]
        return mm.p[k] >= mm.y[i] + mm.y[j] - 1

    m.link_lower = pyo.Constraint(m.P, rule=link_lower_rule)
    m.link_upper = pyo.Constraint(m.P, rule=link_upper_rule)
    m.link_both = pyo.Constraint(m.P, rule=link_both_rule)

    # For each pair, D <= distance(pair) if both selected else D <= large + big-M slack
    def min_dist_rule(mm, k):
        i, j = pair_map[k]
        # use the (lower->higher) directed entry from data consistently for each unordered pair
        dij = d["dist"][(i, j)] * scale
        return mm.D <= dij + M * (1 - mm.p[k])

    m.min_dist = pyo.Constraint(m.P, rule=min_dist_rule)

    m.obj = pyo.Objective(expr=m.D, sense=pyo.maximize)
    return m
